name: ISO 27001
certifications: CQI and IRCA Certified ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Lead Auditor course (PR373)
CQI and IRCA Certified ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Auditor Conversion course (PR374)
IRCA ISMS Auditor and Lead Auditor grades

beginner.summary: For new ISMS team members, control owners and consultants who have not built an information security management system before. Covers the structure of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 with Amendment 1:2024 and clauses 4 to 10, the 93 Annex A controls in four themes, context and interested parties, the ISMS scope, leadership and the information security policy, a first risk assessment and treatment, the Statement of Applicability, documented information, awareness, how certification audits work and what changed from the 2013 edition, all applied to one case company.
prerequisites: Works in IT, security, risk, compliance, operations or a business team that handles information
Can use Microsoft Excel, Word and SharePoint or similar office tools
Has access to the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 27002:2022 texts through the training provider
outcomes: Explain every clause from 4 to 10 and find the right Annex A control for a real practice
Write the scope, context, interested parties register, policy and objectives for an ISMS
Run a first risk assessment, draft a risk treatment plan and build a Statement of Applicability
Control ISMS documents, plan awareness and describe each step of a certification audit

days.topic: ISO/IEC 27001 Overview: Structure, Clauses 4 to 10 and the Case Company
subtopics: What an information security management system is and what an ISO/IEC 27001 certificate covers
Confidentiality, integrity and availability of information
The current edition: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 with Amendment 1:2024
The harmonised structure shared with ISO 9001, ISO 22301 and ISO/IEC 42001
Requirements in clauses 4 to 10 compared with the reference controls in Annex A
How to read ISO wording: shall, should, may and can
The 27000 family: 27000 overview, 27002 controls, 27003 guidance, 27005 risk and 27006-1 certification
Where definitions live now that ISO/IEC 27000:2026 is an overview, and the ISO Online Browsing Platform
Plan-Do-Check-Act and continual improvement in an ISMS
The case company Ledgerline: 420 staff, offices in Bengaluru, Pune and London, and a payments platform on AWS
days.lab_task: Read clauses 4 to 10 and build a clause map in Excel with one row for each of the 30 lowest-level subclauses from 4.1 to 10.2, marking its Plan-Do-Check-Act phase, whether documented information is required and which Ledgerline role would own it.
days.deliverable: Clause map workbook with 30 subclauses, PDCA phases, documented information flags and proposed owners
checks: Count the rows in the clause map
30 subclauses from 4.1 to 10.2 are listed with none missing
Mark the subclauses that require documented information
Subclauses such as 4.3, 5.2, 6.1.3, 6.2 and 9.2.2 are flagged as required
Ask whether Annex A controls are mandatory requirements
Answer explains that Annex A is compared against in 6.1.3 c) and that any exclusion needs a justification in the Statement of Applicability
Written answer in the workbook notes
objectives: Explain what an ISMS is and what certification covers
Find any requirement in clauses 4 to 10
Describe the case company the course builds an ISMS for

days.topic: Annex A: The 93 Controls in Four Themes
subtopics: Organisational controls 5.1 to 5.37
People controls 6.1 to 6.8
Physical controls 7.1 to 7.14
Technological controls 8.1 to 8.34
The 11 controls new in 2022, such as 5.7 threat intelligence, 5.23 cloud services and 8.28 secure coding
How ISO/IEC 27002:2022 adds a purpose and implementation guidance to each control
The five ISO/IEC 27002 attribute types: control type, security properties, cybersecurity concepts, operational capabilities and security domains
Reading one control: control text, purpose, guidance and other information
tools: Microsoft Excel filters and pivot tables
days.lab_task: Sort 40 practices observed at Ledgerline, such as badge entry at the Pune office, MFA on Microsoft 365 and background checks for new joiners, into Annex A control numbers, then use the ISO/IEC 27002 attributes to filter out which of them are detective controls.
days.deliverable: Practice-to-control mapping of 40 Ledgerline practices with theme, control number and attributes
checks: Count controls per theme in the reference sheet
37 organisational, 8 people, 14 physical and 34 technological controls, 93 in total
Map the practice 'staff badge in at the Pune office reception'
Filter the mapping by the control type attribute Detective
Controls such as 8.15 Logging, 8.16 Monitoring activities and 7.4 Physical security monitoring are returned
objectives: Name the four themes and their control ranges
Find the right Annex A control for a real practice

days.topic: Clause 4.1: Internal and External Issues, Including Climate Change
subtopics: What an issue is in clause 4.1 and how it affects the intended outcomes of the ISMS
External issues: law, market, technology, threats and suppliers
Internal issues: culture, structure, systems, skills and contractual commitments
PESTLE and SWOT as ways to find issues
Amendment 1:2024: deciding whether climate change is a relevant issue
Linking issues to the risk assessment in clause 6.1
Keeping the issues list current through management review
Evidence an auditor expects for clause 4.1
days.lab_task: Run a 45-minute PESTLE and SWOT workshop for Ledgerline, record at least 12 internal and external issues with their effect on the ISMS, and write a dated decision on whether climate change is relevant, considering monsoon flooding near the Bengaluru server room and climate questions in bank customer due-diligence forms.
days.deliverable: Issues register with at least 12 issues and a recorded climate change decision
checks: Review each issue in the register
Every issue states how it affects the ISMS outcomes, not just a fact about the world
Look for the climate change decision
A dated decision says whether climate change is relevant and why
Register entry approved by the ISMS manager
Trace one issue into risk thinking
The DPDP Rules duties that apply from May 2027 appear as a source of risk
objectives: Identify internal and external issues for an ISMS

days.topic: Clause 4.2: Interested Parties and Their Requirements
subtopics: Who counts as an interested party: customers, regulators, staff, suppliers, investors and the public
Relevant interested parties compared with every possible stakeholder
Turning needs and expectations into requirements
Clause 4.2 c): deciding which requirements the ISMS will address
Legal and regulatory requirements: the DPDP Act 2023, the IT Act 2000 with CERT-In Directions, and GDPR
Contractual requirements from customer security schedules
The 2024 note that interested parties can have climate change requirements
Keeping the register linked to control 5.31 on legal and contractual requirements
days.lab_task: Build a register of 12 interested parties for Ledgerline, including bank customers, CERT-In, the Data Protection Board of India, AWS and staff, record at least 20 of their requirements, and mark which ones the ISMS will address and how.
days.deliverable: Interested parties register with 20 requirements and a clause 4.2 c) decision for each
checks: The duty to report listed incident types within 6 hours is recorded
A customer clause such as an annual penetration test is listed with its contract reference
Each requirement is marked as addressed through the ISMS or not, with a reason
objectives: Record legal, regulatory and contractual requirements
Decide which requirements the ISMS addresses

days.topic: Defining the ISMS Scope and Its Interfaces
subtopics: Clause 4.3: boundaries and applicability of the ISMS
Using the issues from 4.1 and the requirements from 4.2 to set the scope
Organisational, physical, logical and process boundaries
Interfaces and dependencies with activities done by other organisations
Why a narrow scope can fail customer expectations
Writing the scope statement that will appear on the certificate
Clause 4.4: the ISMS processes and how they interact
How auditors test the scope during stage 1
tools: AWS architecture diagram of the LedgerPay platform
days.lab_task: Write Ledgerline's scope statement covering the LedgerPay platform, the Bengaluru and Pune offices and the HR, IT and customer support functions, draw a boundary diagram with eight interfaces such as AWS, the Chennai support BPO and the London sales office, and list the dependency each interface creates.
days.deliverable: Scope statement, boundary diagram and interface and dependency list
checks: Ask what is excluded and why
The London sales office exclusion is justified and its interface with the ISMS is controlled
AWS is shown as an external dependency with the shared responsibility split noted
One or two sentences name the services, sites and activities in scope
objectives: Write a scope statement fit for a certificate

days.topic: Leadership Commitment and ISMS Roles
subtopics: Clause 5.1 a) to h): what top management must show
Integrating ISMS requirements into business processes
Providing resources and directing and supporting people
Clause 5.3: assigning and communicating responsibilities and authorities
ISMS manager, risk owners, control owners and asset owners
An information security steering committee and its terms of reference
Segregation of duties (5.3) and management responsibilities (5.4) in Annex A
Evidence of leadership an auditor looks for
days.lab_task: Prepare a RACI matrix for 15 ISMS activities at Ledgerline and terms of reference for a steering committee chaired by the COO, then role-play a 20-minute meeting in which the CEO approves an ISMS budget of INR 85 lakh and the ISMS manager's authority.
days.deliverable: RACI matrix, steering committee terms of reference and approved meeting minutes
checks: Check each activity in the RACI
Exactly one accountable role per activity
Roles appear in job descriptions or on an intranet page with a publication date
Budget, resources and the ISMS manager's authority are recorded as decisions
objectives: Explain top management duties under clause 5

days.topic: Writing the Information Security Policy
subtopics: Clause 5.2 a) to g): what the policy must contain
Objectives in the policy or a framework for setting them
Commitments to meet applicable requirements and to improve continually
Topic-specific policies under control 5.1
Policy hierarchy: policy, topic-specific policies, standards and procedures
Approval, communication and availability to interested parties
Review at planned intervals and after significant change
Common audit findings on policies
days.lab_task: Draft a two-page information security policy for Ledgerline that meets clause 5.2 a) to g), list the 10 topic-specific policies the company needs, such as access control and acceptable use, and publish the approved policy on SharePoint with a Microsoft Forms acknowledgement for staff.
days.deliverable: Approved information security policy and a topic-specific policy list
checks: Map the policy against 5.2 a) to g)
Each item from a) to g) is covered by a sentence in the policy
The policy shows the CEO's approval, version 1.0 and the next review date
Ask a participant where staff find the policy
A link to the SharePoint page and the acknowledgement form is given
objectives: Write a policy that meets clause 5.2

days.topic: Information Security Objectives and Planning Changes
subtopics: Clause 6.2: objectives consistent with the policy and measurable where practicable
Taking requirements and risk results into account
Planning what will be done, resources, who, when and how results are evaluated
Monitoring, communicating and updating objectives
Examples: patching times, phishing report rates and supplier review coverage
Clause 6.3: carrying out changes to the ISMS in a planned way
Recording a planned change, such as moving an office inside the scope
Keeping objectives available as documented information
days.lab_task: Set five measurable information security objectives for Ledgerline, for example 'patch critical vulnerabilities on internet-facing systems within 14 days in 95% of cases by March', each with an owner, resources, deadline and evaluation method, and plan the move of the Pune development centre to a new building as an ISMS change under clause 6.3.
days.deliverable: Objectives plan with five objectives and a planned change record for the Pune move
checks: Check each objective for a measure
Each has a number, a target date and a data source
Trace an objective to the policy or a risk
Each objective links to a policy commitment or a risk ID
Review the change plan for the Pune move
Purpose, effect on controls, resources and owner are recorded before the move date
objectives: Plan how objectives are achieved and evaluated

days.topic: Information Asset Inventory and Classification
subtopics: Control 5.9: inventory of information and other associated assets
Primary assets such as information and processes, and supporting assets such as systems, people and sites
Asset owners and their duties
Control 5.12: a classification scheme based on confidentiality, integrity and availability needs
Control 5.13: labelling information
Controls 5.10 acceptable use and 5.11 return of assets
Pulling asset data from Microsoft Intune and AWS Config
Keeping the inventory accurate as things change
days.lab_task: Build an asset register of 40 Ledgerline assets, including the LedgerPay customer database, the GitHub repositories and 25 laptops exported from Intune, give each a named owner and a level from a four-level scheme (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted), and apply a Purview sensitivity label to two sample documents.
days.deliverable: Asset register of 40 assets with owners and classifications, plus two labelled documents
checks: Each has a named person as owner, not a team name
Classify the card token vault database
Classified Restricted with a written reason
The Confidential label shows in the header and in the file properties

days.topic: Risk Criteria and the Risk Assessment Method
subtopics: Clause 6.1.1: risks and opportunities for the ISMS itself
Clause 6.1.2 a): risk acceptance criteria and criteria for performing assessments
Clause 6.1.2 b): consistent, valid and comparable results
Likelihood and consequence scales with plain descriptions
A 5 by 5 risk matrix and risk levels
Who can accept which level of risk
Documenting the risk assessment process as required documented information
Choosing a method that suits a 420-person company
days.lab_task: Write Ledgerline's risk assessment method: define five likelihood levels and five consequence levels with financial, customer, legal and reputational descriptions, set the acceptance threshold at a score of 8 or below, and state who approves risks scored 15 or above.
days.deliverable: Risk assessment method document with scales, matrix and acceptance criteria
checks: Two participants score the same risk with the method
Their scores match or differ by one level at most
The threshold and the approver for each level are written down
Each level has a measurable example such as an INR loss band or hours of outage
objectives: Write a repeatable risk assessment method

days.topic: Ledgerline's First Information Risk Assessment
subtopics: Identifying risks to confidentiality, integrity and availability within the scope
Using assets, threats and vulnerabilities to find risks
Naming a risk owner for each risk under 6.1.2 c)
Analysing consequences and likelihood under 6.1.2 d)
Evaluating and prioritising risks against the criteria under 6.1.2 e)
Running a risk workshop with process owners
Recording results as documented information under clause 8.2
First-time mistakes: missing controls written as risks and risks without owners
days.lab_task: Run a 90-minute workshop with the platform, HR and support leads, identify at least 15 risks to the LedgerPay service, such as ransomware on the Pune build servers and misuse of support tool access at the BPO, then score, evaluate and rank them with named risk owners.
days.deliverable: Risk register with 15 assessed and ranked risks and their owners
checks: Each names an asset or process, a threat and a consequence
Sort the register by risk score
Risks above the acceptance threshold are flagged for treatment
Each risk has an owner with the authority to approve its treatment
objectives: Identify risks within the ISMS scope
Analyse and evaluate risks with the agreed method

days.topic: Risk Treatment Options and Control Selection
subtopics: Clause 6.1.3 a): choosing risk treatment options
Modifying, retaining, avoiding and sharing risk
Clause 6.1.3 b): determining all controls needed for the chosen option
Clause 6.1.3 c): comparing with Annex A so that no necessary control is missed
Controls from other sources, such as the CIS Controls or customer contracts
Drafting a first risk treatment plan under 6.1.3 e)
Risk owners approving the plan and accepting residual risk under 6.1.3 f)
Recording treatment results under clause 8.3
days.lab_task: Choose a treatment option for Ledgerline's top 8 risks, list the controls for each with Annex A references, draft the risk treatment plan with owners, dates and costs, and record each risk owner's approval of the residual risk.
days.deliverable: Risk treatment plan for 8 risks with control references and residual risk approvals
checks: Check the option chosen for the BPO access risk
Option is modify, with controls such as 5.18, 5.20 and 8.15 listed
Look for the Annex A comparison
The comparison step is recorded and no necessary control was overlooked
Each risk owner's approval is recorded with a date
objectives: Select necessary controls and compare them with Annex A

days.topic: Building the Statement of Applicability
subtopics: Clause 6.1.3 d): what the Statement of Applicability must contain
Necessary controls and the justification for including them
Whether each necessary control is implemented or not
Justifying the exclusion of Annex A controls
Linking SoA rows to risks, requirements and documents
Version control and approval of the SoA
How the certificate refers to the SoA version
Common SoA mistakes auditors find
days.lab_task: Build Ledgerline's SoA for all 93 Annex A controls, giving for each the inclusion or exclusion decision, the justification, the implementation status and the link to a risk or requirement, and justify excluding 8.30 outsourced development if the CTO confirms that no development is outsourced.
days.deliverable: Statement of Applicability version 0.9 for 93 controls with justifications and status
checks: Count the rows in the SoA
Excluded with the reason that no development is outsourced, confirmed by the CTO
Pick an included control and trace it
It links to at least one risk ID or interested party requirement
objectives: Build an SoA that meets 6.1.3 d)
Link controls to risks and requirements

days.topic: Documented Information and Document Control
subtopics: Clause 7.5.1: information the standard requires and information the organisation decides it needs
The list of mandatory documents and records with clause references
Clause 7.5.2: identification, format, review and approval
Clause 7.5.3: distribution, access, storage, change control, retention and disposition
Documents of external origin, such as customer contracts and ISO standards
Version numbering and document control tables
SharePoint libraries, versioning, permissions and retention labels
Keeping documentation lean for a mid-sized company
days.lab_task: Set up a SharePoint ISMS library for Ledgerline with columns for owner, version, review date and classification, load the documents written so far, list the mandatory documented information with its clause reference, and apply a retention label that keeps internal audit records for 3 years.
days.deliverable: ISMS document register and a configured SharePoint library
checks: Version moves from 1.0 to 1.1 and the earlier version stays in history
It includes scope, policy, risk processes, SoA, objectives, competence evidence, audit programme and results, management review results and corrective action records
Try to edit a document as a standard user
Editing is refused because only owners can edit
objectives: Run a document library for the ISMS

days.topic: Competence, Awareness and Communication
subtopics: Clause 7.1: resources for the ISMS
Clause 7.2: deciding the competence needed and keeping evidence of it
Clause 7.3: what every person doing work under the organisation's control must be aware of
Control 6.3: awareness, education and training programmes
Phishing simulations and how to read their results
Clause 7.4: what, when, with whom and how to communicate
Measuring awareness with quiz scores and phishing report rates
Induction and yearly refresher training
tools: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Attack simulation training
days.lab_task: Build a competence matrix for 8 ISMS roles at Ledgerline, write a 12-month awareness plan, create a 10-question Microsoft Forms quiz on the policy, and send a simulated phishing email to a test group of 20 users with Attack simulation training.
days.deliverable: Competence matrix, awareness plan, quiz results and phishing simulation report
checks: Review the competence evidence for the ISMS manager
A certificate or training record is attached, not just a statement
Click rate and report rate for the 20 test users are shown
Each item states what, when, with whom and how

days.topic: Clause 8: Operating the ISMS Day to Day
subtopics: Clause 8.1: planning, implementing and controlling processes
Setting criteria for processes and keeping evidence they ran as planned
Controlling planned changes and reviewing unintended ones
Controlling externally provided processes, products and services
Clause 8.2: repeating risk assessments at planned intervals and after significant change
Clause 8.3: carrying out the risk treatment plan
An ISMS operating calendar of monthly, quarterly and yearly tasks
Evidence logs for recurring controls
days.lab_task: Create Ledgerline's 12-month ISMS operating calendar with at least 20 recurring activities, such as quarterly access reviews and monthly backup restore tests, raise Jira tickets for the first month's tasks, and record the evidence for two of them.
days.deliverable: ISMS operating calendar and two completed evidence records
checks: Each activity has a frequency, an owner and an evidence location
Close the Jira ticket for a backup restore test
The ticket shows the restore result and a screenshot
Ask when the risk assessment is repeated
Answer gives the planned interval and triggers such as a new product or a major incident

days.topic: Clauses 9 and 10: Monitoring, Audit, Review and Improvement
subtopics: Clause 9.1: what to monitor and measure, methods, timing and who analyses
Clause 9.2: the internal audit programme and objective auditors
Clause 9.3: management review inputs and outputs
Clause 10.1: continual improvement
Clause 10.2: reacting to nonconformities and correcting them
Correction compared with corrective action
Finding a root cause in simple terms
Records required for clauses 9 and 10
days.lab_task: Write a monitoring table for six measures, audit clause 7.5 of the Ledgerline ISMS in pairs with a 10-question checklist, raise one nonconformity, and draft a management review agenda that lists every input in clause 9.3.2.
days.deliverable: Monitoring table, a completed audit checklist with one nonconformity, and a management review agenda
checks: Each measure states method, frequency, who measures and who analyses
It quotes the requirement, the evidence and what was missing
Inputs a) to g) all appear, including changes in interested parties' needs
objectives: Explain the requirements of clauses 9 and 10
Carry out a small internal audit

days.topic: How ISO/IEC 27001 Certification Audits Work
subtopics: Certification bodies, accreditation bodies such as NABCB and UKAS, and the IAF
ISO/IEC 17021-1 and ISO/IEC 27006-1:2024 in plain terms
Stage 1: documents, readiness and planning stage 2
Stage 2: checking implementation and effectiveness
Major and minor nonconformities and opportunities for improvement
The three-year cycle: surveillance audits and recertification
How audit duration depends on the number of people in scope
Checking a certificate in IAF CertSearch
tools: NABCB and UKAS directories of accredited certification bodies
days.lab_task: Compare two certification body proposals for Ledgerline, check one sample certificate in IAF CertSearch, and read a mock stage 1 report to list three findings that would delay stage 2.
days.deliverable: Certification body comparison, a verified certificate record and a stage 1 findings list
checks: Check whether each certification body is accredited for ISO/IEC 27001
The accreditation body and the accredited scope are confirmed
Look up a certificate in IAF CertSearch
Certificate status, scope and expiry date are shown
The first surveillance audit is within 12 months of the certification decision

days.topic: Transition from ISO/IEC 27001:2013 to 2022 and Amendment 1
subtopics: Why the 2022 edition was published and what stayed the same
From 114 controls in 14 domains to 93 controls in four themes
The 11 new controls and the 2013 controls that were merged
Clause changes: 4.2 c), 4.4, 6.2, the new 6.3, 8.1, and 9.2 and 9.3 split into subclauses
Amendment 1:2024 and climate change in 4.1 and 4.2
The IAF MD 26 deadline of 31 October 2025 and what happened to 2013 certificates
Updating an old SoA with the correspondence tables in ISO/IEC 27002:2022 Annex B
Reading supplier certificates that still show the 2013 edition
days.lab_task: Convert a 2013-style SoA of 114 controls from a small company Ledgerline acquired into the 2022 structure with the ISO/IEC 27002 Annex B tables, list where the 11 new controls need new evidence, and flag any supplier certificate still issued against the 2013 edition.
days.deliverable: Converted SoA, a new-control gap list and a supplier certificate check
checks: Check a supplier certificate issued against the 2013 edition
It is marked as no longer valid after 31 October 2025
objectives: Convert an old SoA to the 2022 structure

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: ISMS Starter Pack for Ledgerline
subtopics: Scope, context and interested parties brought together
Policy, objectives and roles
Risk register, treatment plan and Statement of Applicability
Document register and awareness plan
Readiness check against clauses 4 to 10
Presenting the starter pack to top management
days.lab_task: Assemble the Ledgerline ISMS starter pack from the earlier days, check it against all 30 subclauses of clauses 4 to 10, close at least three gaps, and give a 15-minute briefing asking the CEO to approve planning for stage 1.
days.deliverable: ISMS starter pack with a clause-by-clause readiness checklist and briefing slides
checks: Every subclause is marked met, partly met or not met with evidence
Trace one risk from the register to the SoA
The risk, its controls and the SoA rows agree
Brief the trainer acting as CEO
The CEO approves stage 1 planning or sets conditions
objectives: Combine the beginner ISMS documents into one pack
Present the ISMS to top management

intermediate.summary: For ISMS managers, implementers and security leads who can already explain the clauses and Annex A and now have to make an ISMS work. Covers gap assessment and planning, risk methodology with ISO/IEC 27005, risk treatment plans, implementing organisational, people, physical and technological controls with ISO/IEC 27002, measurement with ISO/IEC 27004, supplier and cloud security with ISO/IEC 27036, 27017 and 27018, incident management, ICT readiness and ISO 22301, privacy with ISO/IEC 27701:2025, internal audit with ISO 19011, management review, corrective action and preparing for stage 1 and stage 2 audits.
prerequisites: Completed the beginner track or can explain clauses 4 to 10 and the four Annex A themes
Has taken part in a risk assessment or written ISMS documents
Works with IT, cloud or security teams and can get read access to their tools
outcomes: Run ISO/IEC 27005 risk assessments and write risk treatment plans that risk owners approve
Implement Annex A controls with ISO/IEC 27002 guidance and keep evidence that they operate
Run internal audits, management reviews and corrective action to the standard
Bring an ISMS to stage 1 and stage 2 readiness with measures, supplier, cloud, incident and privacy controls

days.topic: ISMS Gap Assessment and Implementation Plan
subtopics: Gap assessment against the 30 subclauses and 93 controls
Maturity ratings from 0 to 5 with evidence notes
Sizing gaps in person-days and external cost
Workstreams: governance, risk, controls, people, suppliers and audit
A 9-month plan to stage 1 with milestones and a critical path
Using ISO/IEC 27003 implementation guidance
Choosing between a GRC tool and a document toolkit
Reporting progress to the steering committee
days.lab_task: Assess Ledgerline against all 30 subclauses and 93 controls with a 0-to-5 maturity rating, size each gap in person-days, and build a 9-month plan with six workstreams that reaches stage 1 in month 7.
days.deliverable: Gap assessment, sized gap list and a 9-month implementation plan
checks: All 30 subclauses and 93 controls are rated with evidence notes
Risk assessment and SoA milestones finish before control implementation milestones
Total person-days and external costs are shown by workstream

days.topic: ISO/IEC 27005 Risk Methodology: Event-Based and Asset-Based Identification

Writing risk scenarios

Estimating likelihood from threat intelligence and incident history
Moving results into the risk register and treatment
days.lab_task: Rebuild Ledgerline's risk method to ISO/IEC 27005: write six strategic event-based scenarios, such as an AWS region outage or insider fraud at the BPO, and 20 operational asset-based scenarios, score them in CISO Assistant, and compare the results with the beginner risk register.
days.deliverable: Risk method version 2.0 and 26 assessed risk scenarios in the GRC tool
checks: It names the risk source, the event and the business consequence
It names the asset, threat, vulnerability and existing controls
Compare with the first risk register
At least three new risks are found and two duplicates removed
objectives: Assess risks in a GRC tool

days.topic: Risk Treatment Plans and Residual Risk Acceptance
subtopics: Treatment options in ISO/IEC 27005: modify, retain, avoid and share
Writing a plan with actions, owners, dates and costs
Expected control effect and residual risk
Cost-benefit reasoning for treatment choices
Risk acceptance by risk owners and exceptions with expiry dates
Keeping SoA implementation status in line with the plan
Tracking treatment progress under clause 8.3
Cyber insurance as risk sharing and its limits
days.lab_task: Write treatment plans for Ledgerline's 12 highest risks with 30 actions, estimate the cost and residual risk of each, raise two time-limited risk exceptions, and update SoA implementation status from the plan.
days.deliverable: Risk treatment plan with 30 actions, two signed exceptions and an updated SoA
checks: Owner, due date, cost and the control it implements are recorded
Expiry within 6 months and compensating controls are stated

objectives: Keep the SoA in line with treatment

days.topic: Implementing Organisational Controls with ISO/IEC 27002

advanced.summary: For lead auditors, certification body auditors, ISMS programme leaders and CISOs who already run or audit an ISMS. Covers audit programmes, planning and leading audits, evidence, sampling and remote auditing, writing and grading findings, certification body rules in ISO/IEC 17021-1 and ISO/IEC 27006-1, multi-site and group certification, surveillance, recertification and major nonconformities, alignment with SOC 2, NIST CSF 2.0, India's DPDP Act and GDPR, ISO/IEC 42001 alongside the ISMS, compliance automation, board metrics and running a combined management system.
prerequisites: Has implemented an ISMS or completed the intermediate track
Has taken part in at least one internal, supplier or certification audit of an ISMS
Reads ISO/IEC 27001 clauses and Annex A controls without help
outcomes: Plan, lead and report ISMS certification, internal and supplier audits with sound evidence and sampling
Apply ISO/IEC 17021-1 and ISO/IEC 27006-1 rules to multi-site audits, surveillance, recertification and major nonconformities
Align one ISMS with SOC 2, NIST CSF 2.0, the DPDP Act, GDPR and ISO/IEC 42001
Lead an ISMS programme with GRC automation, maturity measures and board reporting
